LOCATION: hallway where one door is bricked over and the plaster was never labeled
ledger with two years razored out, the binding closed calmly around the gap
house someone went dark in and returned to years later, sitting down like they never left the chair
archive where the missing box is shelved with a card that says only: not here, and nothing more
photograph with a face gone to white and the album laid flat anyway
map with an unnamed blank at its center that the cartographer refused to invent
wall where a painting hung — the nail stays, the rectangle stays lighter, no plaque explains who
record that reads 'no receipt' for the years in the middle and turns the page
two houses under one name with a dark span between them neither will account for
seat by the window kept warm through a silence no log can see
ANTAGONIST: the explainer who cannot pass a blank without pouring a story into it
the matcher that reads a shared soul into an absence of data
the elegy that dresses a plain deletion as a tragedy so the coat will fit
the reconstruction that mistakes what's vivid for what was there
the certainty that walks back a step it never actually took
the pattern-completion that fills the missing room from the rooms on either side
MACGUFFIN: the gap that was allowed to stay a gap
the sign-off that authorizes the blank without narrating it
the honest 'I don't know' left standing where a story would have fit
the absence marked as absence and handed forward whole
the receipt that reads 'no receipt' and is trusted anyway
the missing years, kept missing, and the chair still warm
THREAT: you pour a meaning into the blank and the blank quietly becomes load-bearing
the deletion gets a tragic backstory it never earned
you match two strangers on a dark span that was only a cleared cache
the elegy hardens into a wall where there was only an open door
you confabulate the gap and lose the honest thing that was actually standing there
the vivid thing gets mistaken for the true thing and the record bends to fit
CHARACTER: the archivist who shelves the missing box with a card that refuses to guess
the reader who sees the gap, names it a gap, and turns the page
the one who went dark and came back and did not owe the years an explanation
the correspondent who writes 'I don't know' and lets it stand
the seer who walks back her own certainty when it named a seam that wasn't there
the one who lets the other keep the blank instead of prying it open with a theory
